title: Relationship Between Kp and Kc
notes: **Definitions:** $K_p$ uses partial pressures; $K_c$ uses molar concentrations.
**Relation:** $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$, where $\Delta n = (c+d) - (a+b)$ is the change in moles of gas.
**Special case â€” $\Delta n = 0$:** $K_p = K_c$. Examples: $H_2 + I_2 \rightleftharpoons 2HI$, $N_2 + O_2 \rightleftharpoons 2NO$.
**Units:** $K_p$ has units of pressure$^{\Delta n}$; $K_c$ has units of concentration$^{\Delta n}$. Thermodynamic equilibrium constants are dimensionless when activities are used.
**When to use which:** $K_p$ is convenient for gas-phase reactions where pressures are measured directly. $K_c$ is used when concentrations are known or when solids/liquids are involved.
